key_insight: Training GPT-style models on synthetic limit order book streams reveals that they learn amortized Bayesian inference over hidden market regimes, not just next-token imitation.
engineering_relevance: This suggests foundation models can be used as fast, low-cost estimators and predictors of market microstructure parameters, with potential for regime detection and calibrated simulation.
method: Train autoregressive transformers on synthetic order-flow from simulators with known latent state and entropy.
Compare model predictions to exact Bayes-optimal and oracle predictors under stationary and drifting regimes.
Probe frozen activations to linearly decode latent simulator parameters and test zero-shot transfer to real NASDAQ data.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports near-Bayes-optimal prediction within a millinat per token, strong latent-state decodability, and improved zero-shot transfer when the simulator prior better matches real flow.
watch_item: Results depend on how well the synthetic simulator prior covers real market dynamics, so transfer to unseen markets may degrade if the prior is misspecified.
paper_title: What Do Foundation Models for Market Microstructure Learn? A Controlled Study with Synthetic Limit Order Books
